title: What TypeScript is — quick overview
rememberThis: TypeScript checks types at compile time, then erases them — JavaScript engines never see interfaces.
tsc type-checks and emits .js; many apps run tsc --noEmit in CI plus a fast bundler for emit.
tsconfig strict: true is the baseline for new projects; NodeNext for Node ESM libraries.
Validate external data at run time (Zod, guards) — annotations on JSON.parse do not enforce anything.
C# types survive in IL for the CLR; polyglot systems share OpenAPI/JSON Schema, not TS interfaces.
bullets: TS is a superset of JS — rename .js to .ts and adopt types incrementally with allowJs.
Interfaces and type aliases erase; classes and enums emit JavaScript.
Annotate exported APIs; let const and clear initializers infer.
.d.ts and @types/* describe untyped npm packages to the checker.
tsc is not dotnet build — output is JavaScript, not IL assemblies.
